questions.text: How does a Q-Former reduce the visual token count passed to an LLM?

options.A: It turns each image patch into a separate natural-language sentence.
options.B: It expands each patch into several tokens using a wider projection.
options.C: It uses a fixed set of learned queries to summarize image features.
options.D: It removes the vision encoder and sends raw pixels to the text decoder.

questions.explanation: Learned queries cross-attend to image features, producing one summary token per query rather than one per image patch.

questions.text: In BLIP-2 stage 2, which parameters are trained when connecting the vision features to the frozen LLM?

options.A: The vision encoder and LLM, while the Q-Former stays frozen.
options.B: The Q-Former and output projection, while both backbones stay frozen.
options.C: Only the LLM embedding table, while the full visual bridge stays frozen.
options.D: All model parameters, including both backbones and the visual bridge.

questions.explanation: Stage 2 trains the Q-Former and projection using the generative loss, leaving the vision encoder and LLM weights frozen.

questions.text: The toy uses 8 queries, 64 patches, QUERY_DIM=16, and LLM_DIM=24. What are the attention-weight and projected-output shapes?
questions.explanation: Each query has weights over all 64 patches. Cross-attention preserves the 8-query count; projection changes each output width to 24.
